messages.subject: Problem using aroma.affymetrix in package using S4 classes
parts:
Dear Henrik

I am trying to create a package which uses aroma.affymetrix where I
define the following S4 class:

setClass("AromaSNP",
representation(setname = "",
chipname = "",
celset = "list"),
prototype(setname = "character",
chipname = "character",
celset = list())
)

I have two generic methods where I wrap functions from your
"test20070823" file:

1. readData:
"readData.AromaSNP" <- function(object, verbose = FALSE, ...) {
csList <- list();
for (chiptype in object@chipname) {
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(object@setname,
chipType=chiptype, verbose=verbose);
csList[[chiptype]] <- cs;
}
object@celset <- csList;
return(object);
}
setMethod("readData", "AromaSNP", readData.AromaSNP);

2. normalizeData:
"normalizeData.AromaSNP" <-
function(object, verbose = FALSE, ...) {
csList <- object@celset;
csAccList <- list();
for (chiptype in names(csList)) {
cs <- csList[[chiptype]];
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs);
csAcc <- process(acc, verbose=verbose);
stopifnot(identical(getNames(csAcc), getNames(cs)));
csAccList[[chiptype]] <- csAcc;
}
return(object);
}
setMethod("normalizeData", "AromaSNP", normalizeData.AromaSNP);


When running the package, readData() id ok, but normalizeData() gives
an error:

> aroma <- new("AromaSNP", setname="TestSty250K", chipname="Mapping250K_Sty")
> aroma <- readData(aroma, verbose=T)

My questions are:
1, Is it in principle possible to wrap aroma.affymetrix code in S4

I haven't done it by I cannot see any reason why it should work. All
that is used is good old S3 methods.

> 2, Since the error occurs in "process(acc, verbose=verbose)": Is there
> any information missing,
> which I need to supply so that the genome information is found?

Yes, the error message looks for "genome information" annotation data,
because now the default in AllelicCrosstalkCalibration is to exclude
data points on ChrX & ChrY. Did you try the same code without
wrapping it up?

In order to infer what probes are on what chromosome extra annotation
data is needed. The term "genome information" is the working term
inherited from dChip and the fact that aroma.affymetrix used (and can
still use) dChip's so called "genome information annotation files".
We are now moving towards using UGP files instead, so just make sure
the package can find the corresponding one and everything should be
find. Alternatively you can fit the model using all data points by
using argument 'subsetToAvg=NULL' in AllelicCrosstalkCalibration.

...since I guess you by now know what I was going to write here I skip it ;)

/Henrik

methods :( This was the reason for calling it readData() and not
getData() as I first wanted. So, yes, it is a problem using the same
name.

You can also try to load your package before aroma.affymetrix.

> aroma.affymetrix package would contain a NAMESPACE.

FYI, moving towards using namespaces is not that easy indeed, so it
won't happen anytime soon. I tried to do that with, I think it was,
'aroma' and it didn't take long until there was a lot of problems
reported. Also, since working without a namespace makes it soo much
easier to patch, develop the package, and *troubleshoot and support*
other peoples problems, it is not on the top of my priority list.

> For the moment it would help if I could get an alphabetical list of

> > > I have two generic methods where I wrap functions from your

> > > }
> > > object@celset <- csList;
> > > return(object);
> > > }
> > > setMethod("readData", "AromaSNP", readData.AromaSNP);

> > > 2. normalizeData:
> > > "normalizeData.AromaSNP" <-
> > > function(object, verbose = FALSE, ...) {
> > > csList <- object@celset;
> > > csAccList <- list();
> > > for (chiptype in names(csList)) {
> > > cs <- csList[[chiptype]];
> > > acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs);
> > > csAcc <- process(acc, verbose=verbose);
> > > stopifnot(identical(getNames(csAcc), getNames(cs)));
> > > csAccList[[chiptype]] <- csAcc;
> > > }
> > > return(object);
> > > }
> > > setMethod("normalizeData", "AromaSNP", normalizeData.AromaSNP);

> > > an error:
